title: Control plane: add autoscaling min/max bounds schema + validation for Dedicated pools
creator: Ethan Park
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
Dedicated autoscaling needs strict customer-configured capacity bounds (min/max) that are validated and persisted in the control plane, then evaluated deterministically by the policy engine and consumed by the fleet autoscaler.

This ticket covers:
1) API + persistence schema changes for bounds on DedicatedPool autoscaling config
2) Validation + error messages (customer-facing)
3) Versioning/migration strategy for existing pools

Non-goals (handled in follow-ups)
- Policy evaluation semantics (ENG-2842)
- Autoscaler clamping logic (ENG-2843)
- Backfill job/default bounds for existing pools at scale (ENG-2850)

Proposed schema (control plane)
Add optional bounds to DedicatedPool autoscaling configuration.

Field names (final):
- autoscaling.min_replicas: int (>= 0)
- autoscaling.max_replicas: int (>= 1)

Notes:
- We will use “replicas” in the control plane API to avoid leaking hardware abstraction. Dedicated replica == 1 model-serving worker bound to 1 GPU in current architecture; if/when we support multi-GPU replicas, the policy engine will translate from replicas to GPUs based on pool hardware profile.
- These fields are only meaningful when autoscaling is enabled.

Validation rules
- If either min_replicas or max_replicas is set, both must be set (avoid ambiguous partial config).
- min_replicas <= max_replicas.
- max_replicas must be >= 1.
- min_replicas must be >= 0.
- Upper bound sanity cap: reject max_replicas > 1000 (guardrail to prevent accidental fat-finger; value chosen to be well above any current Dedicated pool sizing). If we need higher, we can raise via config/allowlist.
- If autoscaling is disabled:
  - Reject setting min/max bounds (return 400 with actionable message: “autoscaling must be enabled to set bounds”).

Error message requirements (customer-facing)
- Include the invalid values in the error.
- Use stable error codes for Support macros and Console mapping:
  - AUTOSCALING_BOUNDS_REQUIRED_PAIR
  - AUTOSCALING_BOUNDS_INVALID_RANGE
  - AUTOSCALING_BOUNDS_INVALID_MIN
  - AUTOSCALING_BOUNDS_INVALID_MAX
  - AUTOSCALING_BOUNDS_REQUIRES_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED

Persistence + versioning
- Add columns/fields to DedicatedPool config storage (JSON blob + typed projection) with null default.
- Bump config schema version (v3 -> v4) and add forward-compatible parsing:
  - Old configs without bounds remain valid.
  - New configs persist bounds and return them on GET.

Migration plan
Phase 1 (this ticket):
- Ship schema support with null defaults; no backfill.
- Add migration code path that reads existing pools and writes schema version v4 on next update.
- Add audit log entry on config change (existing mechanism) when bounds are set/updated.

Phase 2 (ENG-2850):
- Backfill defaults for existing pools and communicate to customers.

Acceptance criteria
- Control plane API accepts and persists autoscaling.min_replicas + autoscaling.max_replicas.
- GET returns the persisted values exactly (no normalization in control plane beyond validation).
- Validation rejects invalid configs with stable error code + actionable message.
- Unit tests cover:
  - min/max happy path
  - min > max
  - min negative
  - max < 1
  - only one of min/max set
  - bounds set while autoscaling disabled
  - max > 1000
- Migration/versioning:
  - Old configs without bounds can still be read.
  - Updating an existing pool without bounds does not introduce bounds implicitly.

Implementation notes
- Keep semantics minimal here; do not apply defaults in the API layer. Defaults/cooldowns/etc should be resolved in policy engine evaluation (ENG-2842) for determinism and to keep a single place for “effective config”.
- Coordinate with Console team on field naming to avoid future rename churn.

Links
- Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/autoscaling-policy-api-schema.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/autoscaling-bounds-predictive-prd.json

Rollout
- Behind feature flag/allowlist at the API layer (allow bounds fields only for allowlisted orgs) to reduce accidental early usage before autoscaler enforcement lands.

Risks
- Field naming confusion (min_gpus vs min_replicas). Mitigation: document mapping in the schema doc and keep policy evaluation responsible for hardware translation.
- Customers setting max too low -> throttling. Mitigation: handled via Console warnings + docs; not in this ticket.
